description:
A state-mutating invocation inside a linked non-primary checkout refuses before any repository
write unless the declared stance or an explicit override permits it.

## Background

The command enumeration already classifies every invocation by whether it must open a
repository mutation session. That classification is exhaustive over the command families that
delegate to a sub-enum classifier; five read-only families match their inner enum with a
wildcard, so a new mutating leaf under one of them must be classified deliberately rather than
inherited silently. That predicate, combined with the worktree primitive computed before
dispatch, is exactly the condition a write policy needs, and evaluating it before the
repository mutation session is opened leaves a refusal with no partial state and no event
behind. One command — issue deletion — already refuses in secondary checkouts today, evidence
that the dispatch site is where such a condition belongs.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Under the refusing stance, an invocation that would open a repository mutation session inside a linked non-primary checkout fails before any repository write, leaving that checkout's store and event log untouched.
- [hard] REQ-02: The refusal names the linked checkout, the stance that refused it, and how to permit the operation; its machine-readable form carries the same three facts.
- [hard] REQ-03: A permissive declared stance and an explicit per-invocation override each permit the invocation, and a permitted override leaves its durable audit record behind.
- [hard] REQ-04: Read-only invocations, invocations in the primary checkout, and invocations outside version control succeed under either stance.
- [hard] REQ-05: Existing coverage that mutates from a linked checkout declares the stance it relies on rather than depending on an unstated default.

## Notes

The condition is evaluated at dispatch, before the repository mutation session is opened, so a
refused invocation is not a state change and appends nothing: the append-on-state-change
guarantee is preserved rather than excepted.

The session predicate is deliberately broader than the divergent-history hazard: an invocation
that writes only the shared control plane or machine-local runtime state still classifies as
mutating and refuses under the refusing stance. An over-refusal of that kind is the chosen
behaviour, not a defect.
title: Refuse state-mutating commands in linked worktrees
